purpose: Tiny Instrument Rating Airplane V2 pilot used to validate concept drills, stimulus packets, scenario cases, and mock oral blueprint import shape before broad content generation.

concept.title: Read ceiling and visibility from a METAR

sources.label: AIM
sources.reference: AIM 7-1-30, Key to Aerodrome Forecast and Aviation Routine Weather Report

rapid_fire.shortPrompt: In a METAR, which cloud layers count as a ceiling?
rapid_fire.idealShortAnswer: The lowest broken, overcast, or obscuration layer counts as the ceiling.

multiple_choice.prompt: A METAR reports SCT018 BKN032. What is the reported ceiling?

choices.text: 1,800 feet AGL
3,200 feet AGL
No ceiling is reported
3,200 feet MSL

multiple_choice.explanation: Scattered is not a ceiling; broken at 3,200 feet AGL is the lowest ceiling layer.
commonMisses: Treating scattered clouds as a ceiling.
Calling reported cloud heights MSL instead of AGL.

concept.title: Apply a TEMPO group only during its forecast time window

sources.label: AIM
sources.reference: AIM 7-1-30, TAF format and change groups
sources.notes: Supports TAF change group timing interpretation.

rapid_fire.shortPrompt: When does a TAF TEMPO group apply?
rapid_fire.idealShortAnswer: Only during the valid time window printed with that TEMPO group.

true_false.statement: A TAF TEMPO group describes temporary forecast conditions during its stated valid period.
true_false.explanation: TEMPO is tied to its listed time range and should not be applied to the whole TAF.

concept.title: Recognize standard alternate weather minima for a precision approach

sources.label: 14 CFR
sources.notes: Defines standard IFR alternate weather minima.

fill_blank.prompt: Standard alternate weather minimums for an airport with a precision approach are ceiling ____ feet and visibility ____ statute miles.
fill_blank.explanation: Unless alternate minimums are published, a precision approach alternate needs a 600-foot ceiling and 2 statute miles visibility.

multiple_choice.prompt: No alternate minimums are published. Your alternate has a usable precision approach. Which forecast weather minimum applies?

choices.text: 400-foot ceiling and 1 mile visibility
600-foot ceiling and 2 miles visibility
800-foot ceiling and 2 miles visibility
1,000-foot ceiling and 3 miles visibility

multiple_choice.explanation: For a precision approach alternate, the standard forecast minimum is 600-2 unless another alternate minimum is published.
commonMisses: Using nonprecision 800-2 minimums for a precision approach.

concept.title: Recognize standard alternate weather minima for a nonprecision approach

sources.label: 14 CFR
sources.notes: Defines standard IFR alternate weather minima.

rapid_fire.shortPrompt: What are the standard alternate minimums for a nonprecision approach?
rapid_fire.idealShortAnswer: An 800-foot ceiling and 2 statute miles visibility, unless different alternate minimums are published.

true_false.statement: For an alternate with only a nonprecision approach, the standard forecast minimum is 800-2 unless different alternate minimums apply.
true_false.explanation: The standard nonprecision alternate minimum is 800 feet ceiling and 2 statute miles visibility.

concept.title: Know the VOR operational check interval for IFR use

sources.label: 14 CFR
sources.notes: States VOR equipment check requirements for IFR operations.

fill_blank.prompt: For IFR operations using VOR equipment, the VOR operational check must have been completed within the preceding ____ days.
fill_blank.explanation: The VOR equipment check must be within the preceding 30 days for IFR use.

multiple_choice.prompt: You plan to use VOR navigation under IFR. Your last VOR check was 35 days ago. What is required before relying on it?

choices.text: Nothing; VOR checks are annual.
Complete and record an acceptable VOR operational check.
Only verify the CDI centers during taxi.
Ask ATC to confirm the VOR is monitored.

multiple_choice.explanation: A VOR check older than 30 days does not satisfy the IFR equipment check requirement.
commonMisses: Confusing station monitoring with the aircraft equipment check.

acs.title: Instrument Rating Airplane ACS
acs.taskTitle: Aircraft Systems Related to IFR Operations

concept.title: Know the altimeter and static system inspection interval

sources.label: 14 CFR
sources.notes: States altimeter and static system inspection requirements for IFR.

rapid_fire.shortPrompt: How often must the altimeter and static pressure system be inspected for IFR operations?

true_false.statement: For IFR operations in controlled airspace, the altimeter and static system inspection is due every 24 calendar months.
true_false.explanation: The required inspection interval is within the preceding 24 calendar months.

acs.title: Instrument Rating Airplane ACS
acs.taskTitle: Aircraft Systems Related to IFR Operations

sources.label: 14 CFR
sources.notes: States transponder test and inspection interval.

fill_blank.prompt: A transponder test and inspection under 14 CFR 91.413 is required within the preceding ____ calendar months.
fill_blank.explanation: The transponder inspection interval is 24 calendar months.

multiple_choice.prompt: Your transponder inspection expired last month. Which statement is correct for IFR flight requiring transponder use?

choices.text: The inspection must be current before using that transponder.
The inspection is only required for turbine aircraft.
The inspection is optional if ADS-B Out works.
A VOR check satisfies the transponder inspection.

multiple_choice.explanation: Transponder test and inspection requirements are separate from ADS-B and navigation equipment checks.
commonMisses: Substituting ADS-B status for the transponder inspection requirement.

acs.title: Instrument Rating Airplane ACS
acs.areaTitle: Air Traffic Control Clearances and Procedures

concept.title: Respond when reaching a clearance limit without further clearance

sources.label: AIM
sources.notes: Supports clearance limit and holding expectations.

coaching.openerPrompt: ATC clears you to a fix and you reach that clearance limit without further clearance. What should your plan include?
hintSequence: Explain holding or expected further clearance logic.
teachingPoints: Do not proceed beyond the clearance limit without authorization.
Clarify or request further clearance before reaching the limit when possible.
expectedAnswerElements: Hold as instructed or as published/appropriate.

rapid_fire.idealShortAnswer: The fix, point, or airport to which an aircraft is cleared when issued an ATC clearance.

multiple_choice.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes MDA from DA?

choices.text: MDA is a hard altitude floor unless visual references allow descent; DA is where the decision is made to continue or miss.
DA applies only to circling approaches; MDA applies only to ILS approaches.
MDA and DA mean the same thing operationally.
MDA is always lower than DA.

multiple_choice.explanation: MDA is not descended below until requirements are met; DA/DH is the decision point on approaches that use it.
commonMisses: Treating MDA and DA as interchangeable.

rapid_fire.shortPrompt: Can you descend below MDA before meeting the required visual-reference conditions?
rapid_fire.idealShortAnswer: No. You must remain at or above MDA until the required conditions for descent are met.

concept.title: Apply the AVE-F and MEA lost-communications priorities

sources.label: 14 CFR
sources.notes: Defines route and altitude rules for IFR two-way radio communications failure.

coaching.openerPrompt: You lose communications in IMC after being assigned a route and altitude. How do you choose the route and altitude to fly?
hintSequence: Separate route priority from altitude priority.
Use assigned, vectored, expected, and filed for route.
Use the highest of MEA, expected, or assigned for altitude.
teachingPoints: Route and altitude priorities are separate.
The answer must use the regulation rather than preference.
expectedAnswerElements: Highest of MEA, expected, assigned altitude.
Continue under 91.185 if VFR cannot be maintained.

multiple_choice.prompt: For IFR lost communications altitude selection, which altitude should you fly?

choices.text: The lowest published altitude for the route only
The highest of the minimum IFR altitude, expected altitude, or assigned altitude
The altitude filed in the flight plan in every case
Any VFR cruising altitude

multiple_choice.explanation: 91.185 uses the highest of the applicable minimum IFR altitude, expected altitude, or assigned altitude.
commonMisses: Confusing route priority with altitude priority.

stimulusPackets.learnerDescription: A METAR/TAF text packet for a preflight IFR weather and alternate-planning discussion.
stimulusPackets.aiContext: The learner sees a METAR with 6 statute miles visibility, a broken ceiling at 2,500 feet AGL, gusty southerly wind, and a TAF showing temporary 3 statute miles visibility with an overcast 900-foot ceiling during the proposed arrival window. The AI should use these decoded values directly and should not infer weather from imagery.
keyDetails: Arrival timing overlaps the temporary lower ceiling.
interpretationNotes: Ask whether the learner applies the TEMPO group to the correct time window.
Use the decoded ceiling and visibility when discussing alternate requirements.

assets.instructions: Display as preformatted aviation weather text.

stimulusPackets.learnerDescription: A simplified approach-minimums excerpt showing DA and visibility values for an ILS approach.
stimulusPackets.aiContext: The learner sees an ILS minimums excerpt with DA 5,420 feet MSL and required visibility 1/2 SM. The airport elevation is 5,280 feet MSL. The AI should explain that DA is the decision point and should not assume any other chart details beyond the displayed excerpt.
interpretationNotes: Use this stimulus to test DA/DH versus MDA language.
Do not ask chart-briefing questions that require omitted plan-view or profile-view data.
commonMisreads: Treating the simplified excerpt as a complete approach plate.

assets.instructions: Display as a small approach-minimums excerpt. The AI context contains the full meaning of the image.

metadata.altText: Simplified ILS minimums excerpt showing DA 5420 and visibility one-half statute mile.

links.usage: Identify DA as a decision point rather than a descent floor.

scenarioCases.title: IFR weather trend and alternate decision
scenarioCases.summary: A two-step scenario where the learner interprets weather, applies alternate logic, and explains a conservative diversion posture.
scenarioCases.aiInstructions: Run this as a guided scenario. Let the learner reason aloud, then ask the checkpoint prompts only when needed. Do not invent weather or chart facts beyond the linked stimulus packets.

steps.title: Decode the weather trend
steps.scenarioText: You are planning an IFR arrival at KAPA during the period covered by the provided METAR/TAF packet.
steps.aiPrompt: Ask the learner what ceiling and visibility values matter for the proposed arrival window.
expectedPilotActions: Apply the TAF TEMPO group only to its valid window.
riskPoints: Ignoring a temporary low ceiling during the arrival window.
Treating the current METAR as the whole forecast.

checkpoints.prompt: Which reported ceiling and visibility values are you using for the arrival decision?
checkpoints.aiEvaluationNotes: Credit answers that identify both the current METAR and the lower temporary forecast conditions.

steps.title: Choose an alternate posture
steps.scenarioText: Your destination weather may remain legal but is trending down near your arrival time. You are considering an alternate with only a nonprecision approach.
steps.aiPrompt: Ask the learner how they would decide whether the alternate is legal and operationally useful.
expectedPilotActions: Use the correct nonprecision alternate minimum.
Separate legal minimums from personal risk management.
Explain a conservative go/no-go or diversion trigger.
riskPoints: Treating legality as the only risk-control decision.

checkpoints.prompt: What standard forecast weather minimum applies to the nonprecision alternate if no different alternate minimum is published?
expectedAnswerElements: unless different alternate minimums are published
checkpoints.aiEvaluationNotes: This checkpoint tests the specific 800-2 data point, not broad weather judgment.

mockOralBlueprints.title: IRA preflight and approach mini mock oral
mockOralBlueprints.examinerStyle: Practical, direct, and scenario-led. Ask concise follow-ups and require the learner to commit to a decision when risk is involved.
mockOralBlueprints.aiInstructions: Use authored concepts, stimulus packets, and scenario cases only. Keep the session oral and adaptive, but do not create new facts, chart data, or weather values beyond the selected content.
